main_text.p: D. Just. & jur. Neque enim qui supremâ in terris gaudet potestate, quicquam adversus jus naturale potest, aut tollere ea quæ naturalis inducit necessitas. Arg. §. 2. v. ergo Senatus. Inst. de Usufr. Vasq. Illustr. quæst. l. 1. c. 18. in init. Arum. disc. public. jur. 18.

Utimprobandum sit hâc in parte jus Saxonicum, quo er-jam[?] qui moderamen adhibuit, in 6o[?]. Solidos, & Werigeldum, uti id appellant, interfecti cognatis præstandum, condemnatur. Zobel. differ. jur. & Saxon. part. 4. diss. 29. Benedict. Reinch. in addit. seut. Scab. L psens. 146. ibid. Berlich. part. 4. concl. 12. n. 4.
In nullo enim peccasse videri potest, qui quod omnes suadent leges, non omisit. l. 3. D. Just. & jur. l. 1. Cod. Unde vi.
Ut cum nullum hîc sit deli-ctum,

page.notes: The word "Utimprobandum" is printed without a space; transcribed as printed. "er-jam" at the line end of the Saxon paragraph is uncertain, and "6o" may be an old-style numeral or a letter o; both are marked. The ligature in "ctum" (deli-ctum) looks like "st" in the scan and is doubtful. Stains and show-through at the right edge are not transcribed.
